answer: A sybil farmer's cheapest move is minting an ocean of shells at once — identities with no past. Force every identity through a sequential proof-of-elapsed chain: each epoch it must publish a VDF output anchored to the previous one, strictly sequential, impossible to parallelize or backfill. New chains earn at the nadir of the reward curve; only unbroken chains months old climb the full ridge. The farmer burns one real-time computation per shell, so cost scales linearly while time can't be bought — and a burst of fresh chains at a reward peak stands out instantly.
